Subject: Acme POC - evaluation plan & success criteria (recap + next steps)

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposal so we have alignment before we kick off the POC:

Success criteria (what Acme needs to validate):
- Accuracy: intent/classification F1 >= 0.85 on the labeled test set (500 examples to start; you mentioned 1,000 might be possible)
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency < 200ms for standard conversational requests (seq len ~128)
- Quality: hallucination rate < 1% (as measured by rubric below)
- Cost: per-conversation inference cost target <$0.03 (we'll show cost profile in the report)

Proposed evaluation plan:
1) Offline eval (static test set) — run our evaluation harness on your labeled data (500 examples). Generates per-case scores and aggregate metrics.
2) Online shadow (optional) — shadow mode for 48–72 hours on ~10% of traffic to validate real-world behavior and latency/cost numbers. No responses served to end users.
3) Grading rubric — we will apply a per-example score (0–3): 3=perfect, 2=acceptable with minor issues, 1=requires human edit, 0=incorrect/hallucinatory. Pass threshold: weighted average >= 2.4 (80%).

Timeline (proposed):
- Confirm evaluation data & rubric by 11/24
- Doc/contract (DPA/data access) signed by 11/27
- Offline eval run and results shared by 12/03
- Optional shadow run 12/06–12/08 (if agreed)

Owners:

- Redwood SE: Neha Kapoor (evaluation harness, offline runs, instrumentation)
- Redwood CS: Rishi Malhotra (success criteria validation & rollout plan)

Attachments: acme_poc_eval_plan_v1.pdf (detailed steps), acme_grading_rubric_v1.xlsx (rubric + scoring sheet)

Next steps: Please confirm (1) that the success criteria above match what you need, (2) whether you can share 500 or 1,000 labeled examples for the offline eval, and (3) whether you want the optional 48–72h shadow run. Once confirmed we'll send a kickoff invite and the DPA link.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Neha / Rishi — looping you in to align on the two asks from Acme:

1) Offline eval vs online shadow: proposed differences
- Offline eval: run on static labeled set (500–1,000 examples). Produces per-example quality score (0–3), precision/recall/F1 for intents, confusion matrices, and an estimated tokens-per-response/cost projection. Latency is estimated from model profiler (not live infra) so use estimated p95 numbers. Good for quick baseline and reproducibility.
- Online shadow: run the model in shadow mode against a sample of live traffic (no customer-facing responses). Measures true p95 latency under production load, end-to-end token usage, and captures real-world failure modes (context-length effects, conversational drift). Also useful to validate caching/batching behavior and warm-up characteristics.

2) Grading aggregation for multi-turn dialogs
- We propose per-turn scoring (0–3) and a conversation-level aggregation: weighted average where later-turn responses get 1.5x weight (since relevance tends to degrade). Example: per-turn scores [3,2,2] -> conv score = (3 + 2*1.5 + 2*1.5) / (1 + 1.5 + 1.5) = weighted average.
- Final pass threshold: weighted average >= 2.4 (80%). We will produce both per-turn breakdowns and conversation-level pass/fail so you can triage issues quickly.

Neha, can you confirm that the harness supports weighted aggregation and that we can run the shadow mode on a 10% sampling config?

Rishi, please confirm the success criteria thresholds above are acceptable from a customer health/rollout standpoint.

Marissa
